title: libdvdcss2 removed by MakeMKV layer autoremove — DVDs can't decrypt (CSS)
description: The MakeMKV build layer in the Dockerfile ends with 'apt-get autoremove -y', which removes libdvdcss2 (and libdvd-pkg) as orphans since HandBrake dlopens libdvdcss at runtime (no hard dpkg dependency). Result: CSS-encrypted DVDs can't be decrypted — HandBrake enumerates titles via libdvdnav but prints 'Encrypted DVD support unavailable / No css library available', and /api/scan returns 0 usable titles; rips would fail. Regression introduced with the Blu-ray feature (the makemkv layer). Pre-Blu-ray image had libdvdcss (user ripped 8 DVDs). Fix: apt-mark manual libdvdcss2 libdvd-pkg before the autoremove (keep them), rebuild, verify libdvdcss present + DVD scan returns titles.
close_reason: Fixed: libdvdcss now built in a dedicated Dockerfile layer after the makemkv autoremove. Verified on real hardware — libdvdcss2 1.4.3 installed, DVD scan returns 27 titles (was 0), main feature detected.

title: Blu-ray scan fails: SCSI-generic node mapped to wrong container path
description: makemkvcon reports 'no usable optical drives' (TCOUNT:0) on some Blu-rays, so /api/scan silently falls back to the DVD scanner and shows 'no titles found'. Root cause: docker-compose.yml hardcodes the sg device container target to /dev/sg1, but the container shares the host sysfs, so MakeMKV derives the sg name from /sys/block/sr0/device/scsi_generic/ (a HOST name, e.g. sg0) and opens that exact path. When the host node isn't sg1, /dev/sgN inside the container doesn't match and MakeMKV can't open the drive. The host sg number shifts across reboots/USB reconnects, which is why one rip worked and later ones failed. Fix: map BD_SG_DEVICE to the same path on both sides of the device mapping. Confirmed by mknod /dev/sg0 in the live container -> makemkvcon then found the disc (TCOUNT:18, The Blind Side).

title: Rip completion notifications silently dropped (dangling asyncio task)
description: ripper._save_record schedules push.notify via asyncio.create_task() but discards the task handle. Per asyncio docs the loop keeps only a weak ref, so the un-retained task can be GC'd before the network-bound webpush send completes -> real-rip notifications silently lost. Awaited paths (manual /api/push/test, diagnostics) work, so it looked fine. Confirmed: pipeline delivers to phone on a direct send (HTTP 201, phone displayed it), but the 18:38 rip under the current working container did not notify. Fix: retain task refs in a set + discard on done.
close_reason: Fixed: retain notify task refs in a set + discard on done (asyncio weak-ref GC footgun). 142 tests pass.

title: Blu-ray output: use MKV container (soft PGS subs + lossless audio)

Plex Direct Plays/Direct Streams MKV H.264; burning bitmap subs on a client still transcodes (accepted tradeoff). Changes: path extension by disc_format, HandBrake --format av_mkv + drop --optimize for MKV, keep soft subtitle embed. Resolves the PGS-in-MP4 limitation.

title: Blu-ray: PGS subtitles can't be soft-embedded in MP4 (only burned)

In the shakedown, requesting subtitle 1 (English) with burn_forced=false produced an MP4 with ZERO subtitle tracks — HandBrake silently dropped the PGS sub. This conflicts with the user's subtitle preference (embed disc English soft + burn forced). Options: (a) burn English subs into the picture (always-on, not selectable); (b) output MKV for Blu-ray (carries PGS soft + lossless audio; Plex plays MKV but Chromecast may transcode); (c) only burn forced subs on BD, no soft English; (d) OCR PGS->SRT (needs extra tooling). NEEDS USER DECISION.

title: Container: work around makemkv.com DNSSEC SERVFAIL with static hosts entry
description: makemkv.com authoritative DNS is returning SERVFAIL under DNSSEC validation (dig +cd resolves to 88.212.208.67; all validating resolvers fail). makemkvcon's HTTP license/online check then can't resolve the host and the disc scan hangs (99% CPU, no output) — previously misdiagnosed as 'host lost internet'. Add an extra_hosts entry in docker-compose.yml mapping makemkv.com + www.makemkv.com to the +cd-resolved IP so the container bypasses the broken DNSSEC. Port 80 (HTTP) on that IP serves 200; port 443 is closed (MakeMKV check is HTTP). Temporary: remove/refresh once MakeMKV fixes their DNSSEC.
notes: RESOLVED root cause: the hang was NOT (only) DNS. makemkvcon hung at 100% CPU in 'SDF auto' drive-firmware processing for the non-LibreDrive Pioneer BDR-XD08 (known MakeMKV bug on Linux). Fix = sdf_Stop setting (via MAKEMKV_SDF_STOP env -> entrypoint writes it) to run standard AACS mode (fine for 1080p). Also added app_UpdateEnable=0 so makemkvcon never phones home. makemkv.com's DOMAIN REGISTRATION LAPSED (DNSSEC SERVFAIL; only registrar parking page on :80, :443 refused) — that's why SDF/SVQ auto-download can't work; extra_hosts pins a reachable IP so stray lookups fail fast instead of hanging. Scan validated: 11 titles, title 2=main (2:21:37), parser matches real output (new fixture+test). decrypt_title also fixed for stale-MKV overwrite false-negative.
close_reason: Resolved: real cause was the MakeMKV SDF 100%-CPU hang on the non-LibreDrive Pioneer drive, fixed via sdf_Stop + app_UpdateEnable=0 (entrypoint from MAKEMKV_SDF_STOP). extra_hosts kept as DNS-failfast belt-and-suspenders. Full BD+ scan->decrypt->encode validated on The Martian.

title: Guard against overlapping disc scans + cancelable scan
description:
Guard against overlapping disc scans and make an in-flight scan cancelable.

## Problem
/api/scan only rejects (409) while a RIP is active (ripper.is_busy, app/main.py:203); it has no guard against a second SCAN starting while one is already running. The frontend Rescan button (#btn-rescan) is never disabled, so repeated clicks each fire a concurrent /api/scan. Observed live: hitting Rescan a few times on a slow disc piled up 5 concurrent makemkvcon processes on the single optical drive, all thrashing it. On a bad disc a scan can hang for up to 10 min (bluray _INFO_TIMEOUT=600s), so a plain guard alone would lock the UI with no escape.

## Approach (chosen: Approach 1 + separate cancel button)
New app/scan_coordinator.py ScanCoordinator on app.state: tracks scan-in-progress (busy), holds the current scan subprocess handle (register_proc, mirroring bluray.decrypt_title / cd._spawn), clears state in finally, and cancel() kills the live subprocess (does NOT cancel the request task, so HTTP stays clean).

Backend (app/main.py): api_scan wraps the scan sequence in coordinator.run(); ScanBusyError -> 409 "Scan already in progress". Thread register_proc through is_dvd_video / dvd.scan / bluray.detect_and_scan. New POST /api/scan/cancel -> coordinator.cancel(). Rip-enqueue paths (api_rip, api_cd_rip) add a cheap `if coordinator.busy -> 409` (scan->rip protection).

Frontend (app/static/app.js, app/templates/index.html): #btn-rescan disabled/greyed during a scan; a separate #btn-scan-cancel (hidden by default) shows during the scan and POSTs /api/scan/cancel. state.scanCancelled flag makes a cancelled scan render "Scan cancelled" instead of "No titles found". New concurrent-scan 409 renders "Scan already in progress".

## Known limitation / follow-up
cd.is_audio_cd reads the TOC via discid.read() as a blocking in-process call (app/cd.py:47, no executor) -> not killable by cancel, and can block the event loop on a bad TOC. Cancel governs the subprocess probes (lsdvd/makemkvcon/HandBrake), which are the ones that hang for minutes. Follow-up bead: wrap discid.read in asyncio.to_thread. Out of scope here.

## Testing (pytest, fake-spawner convention, no real drive)
ScanCoordinator unit (busy toggles; run rejects when busy; cancel kills fake proc + sets flag; run releases on exception); endpoint (two concurrent /api/scan -> second 409; /api/scan/cancel kills fake long-running proc, coordinator idle after; /api/rip during scan -> 409). Frontend button state is manual/smoke (no JS test harness).

Full design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-05-scan-concurrency-guard-design.md
notes: Implemented on feat/scan-concurrency-guard (5 commits 51aa0c3..0452ace). PR #4: https://github.com/timLP79/dvd-rip/pull/4. All 4 plan tasks reviewed clean; final whole-branch review merge-ready; make test 202 passed. Close on merge.

description: Since the Blu-ray feature, /api/scan always runs 'makemkvcon info' first as the disc-type detector, then falls back to the DVD scanner when it's not a Blu-ray. So every DVD scan pays a slow, pointless makemkvcon analysis pass (CSS DVD that MakeMKV will never rip) before the real HandBrake/lsdvd scan — noticeably sluggish 'weird' behaviour. Fix: add a cheap is_dvd_video(device) probe (lsdvd: reads only VIDEO_TS, fast, fails fast on BD) and only invoke makemkvcon when the disc is NOT a DVD. DVD scans skip makemkvcon entirely; Blu-ray auto-detect preserved.

title: Blu-ray track selection: info-scan indices may not map 1:1 to extracted MKV
description: For Blu-ray, the UI lists tracks from 'makemkvcon info' (e.g. The Martian title 3 = 1 audio + 10 subs), but MakeMKV's default profile saves a SUBSET into the MKV (that title's MKV had 1 audio + 5 subs). HandBrake then encodes the MKV using selection indices that came from the info scan, so high/non-English subtitle or audio indices can point at the wrong stream or a missing one. The common case (English audio + English/forced subs = index 1) aligns correctly because MakeMKV orders the primary tracks first. Fix options: (a) parse the MKV's actual streams post-decrypt and remap, (b) drive MakeMKV's track selection so the MKV matches the scan, or (c) constrain the BD UI to MKV-available tracks. Until then, non-default BD track picks are best-effort.
notes: Discovered during BD shakedown 2026-06-16. HandBrake ignores out-of-range subtitle indices, so a default rip still produces a valid MP4.
close_reason: Won't affect real usage: user only ever selects English subtitles, which are the primary track (index 1) and map correctly between the info scan and the extracted MKV. The 1:1 divergence only manifests for non-English/high-index picks, which won't happen. Reasoning preserved here if usage ever changes.

title: Handle ARccOS-protected DVDs via MakeMKV pipeline (Hancock repro)
description:
ARccOS-protected DVDs (Sony DADC bad-sector protection) are mis-handled by the DVD rip path and need to route through the MakeMKV pipeline like Blu-ray.

## Context
Hit a real ARccOS disc (Hancock, unrated). Diagnosis confirmed 2026-07-05 via lsdvd + HandBrake probes. Keep this disc as the reproduction/test case.

## Problem
/api/scan routes DVDs straight to HandBrake: is_dvd_video() uses an lsdvd probe (app/main.py:212) that succeeds fine on an ARccOS disc, so it never reaches the MakeMKV path. HandBrake then rips /dev/sr0 directly (app/ripper.py:260 _run_dvd_job). Two failures:
1. libdvdnav follows the deliberately-corrupt cell structure and stalls on unreadable sectors.
2. The main-feature heuristic (HandBrake MainFeature, falling back to longest-duration in parse_handbrake_scan, app/dvd.py:148) lands on a DECOY title, not the real feature. On Hancock lsdvd reports "Longest track: 40", but title 40 is a ~1:45 clone/trap; the real feature is title 01 (1:42:12, 38 cells).

## ARccOS detection signatures (observed on Hancock)
- lsdvd + libdvdread emit: "Zero check failed in src/ifo_read.c:570 for vmgi_mat->zero_6" (deliberate VMGI tampering -- the fingerprint).
- HandBrake falls back to "Attempting to retrieve all CSS keys / This can take a _long_ time", grinding VTS_01..VTS_19 sequentially (normal key handshake broken).
- Decoy title farm: 42 titles for a one-movie disc. Real feature title 01 (28 ch / 38 cells); near-duplicate clones titles 40/41/42 (~1:45, 37-40 cells); a fake 1-chapter/1-cell 93-min title 39; a wall of ~2-min/2-cell stubs (titles 15-33).

## Proposed fix (option B)
Route protected DVDs through the existing MakeMKV decrypt -> HandBrake pipeline (reuse the _run_bluray_job flow / bluray.decrypt_title). Trigger either by:
- auto-detection heuristic during scan (zero_6 warning seen, or no sane single main feature / many near-duplicate main-feature-length titles), and/or
- a manual UI override ("this disc is copy-protected -- use MakeMKV").

## Open question / caveat (important)
MakeMKV is NOT a guaranteed easy win on ARccOS DVDs. On Hancock, makemkvcon info pegged 100% CPU for ~6 min and never emitted a TCOUNT / title list within a 560s window (killed before completion). Before shipping option B:
- determine an appropriate timeout for the DVD-via-MakeMKV path (Blu-ray uses _INFO_TIMEOUT=600s in app/bluray.py:171 -- likely too short for the nastier protected DVDs), and
- consider a raw dvdbackup / sector-copy fallback if MakeMKV can't resolve titles.
- validate the whole flow end-to-end on the Hancock disc.

value: Dockerfile gotcha (dvd-rip): NEVER run 'apt-get autoremove' after libdvdcss2 is built. HandBrake dlopens libdvdcss at runtime, so no package declares a hard dpkg dependency on it — autoremove judges it an unused orphan and silently removes it, breaking ALL CSS-DVD decryption (HandBrake then enumerates titles via libdvdnav but returns 0 usable ones: 'Encrypted DVD support unavailable / No css library available'; rips fail). This rode in with the Blu-ray feature's makemkv build layer (which purges build-essential + autoremoves). Fix in place: libdvd-pkg is installed/built in its OWN dedicated Dockerfile layer AFTER the makemkv layer's autoremove. Verify after any Docker change: 'docker run --rm --entrypoint sh dvd-rip-dvd-rip -c "ldconfig -p | grep dvdcss"' must show libdvdcss.so.2. Symptom on hardware: /api/scan returns 0 titles for a DVD even though lsdvd lists them.

dvd-rip gotcha: fire-and-forget asyncio.create_task() must retain a STRONG reference or the task can be garbage-collected mid-flight (asyncio keeps only a weak ref) — silently dropping the work. This bit push notifications: ripper._save_record scheduled push.notify() without keeping the handle, so real-rip completion notifications were lost while awaited paths (manual /api/push/test) worked, masking it. Symptom: phone got NO notification on rip completion, but a direct/manual send returned HTTP 201 and displayed fine. MakeMKV in Docker: the container shares the HOST sysfs, so makemkvcon derives the optical drive's SCSI-generic node name from /sys/block/sr0/device/scsi_generic/ (a host name, e.g. sg0) and opens THAT exact /dev/sgN path. The device mapping in docker-compose.yml must map BD_SG_DEVICE to the SAME path on both sides (host:container), never a fixed target like /dev/sg1. A hardcoded target breaks whenever the host enumerates the drive as a different sgN (shifts across reboots/USB reconnects) -> makemkvcon reports 'no usable optical drives' + TCOUNT:0 -> silent DVD fallback -> 'no titles found'. Fixed in dvd-rip-dm4.

Never run 'make restart', 'make down', or 'make build && make restart' in this project while a HandBrake job is running/queued — it kills the worker and leaves a partial MP4 in OUTPUT_DIR. Always check curl http://localhost:8000/api/jobs first; if status=running or queued, ask the user before proceeding. The Makefile 'check-no-active-jobs' target enforces this with FORCE=1 override.
